reasons: Consent defaults to granted while the check runs or if it fails. The server must enforce consent.
The reply is not shown directly, so a failed reload can leave the question with no answer.
The attach button has no action.

terms.meaning: One saved conversation with the assistant.
Retrieval-augmented generation: the AI answers using the patient's own documents.
A web address the app calls to ask the server for data or to save something.
Permission given by the patient for a specific use of their data.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the chat screen
sections.what: Brings in icons, buttons, the API helper, the patient store and class helpers.
sections.why: Standard setup. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: Message
sections.title: Message shape
sections.what: Describes one chat message: its id, whether the user or the AI wrote it, its text, time, and optional source citations.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps messages in one consistent format on screen.

sections.name: ChatSession
sections.title: Conversation summary shape
sections.what: Describes one past conversation: its id, title and creation date.
sections.why: Likely reason: supplies the side list. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: suggestions
sections.title: Starter questions list
sections.what: Four example questions shown on a new chat. Clicking one fills the input box.
sections.why: Likely reason: helps the user start. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: generateUUID
sections.title: Unique id generator
sections.what: Creates a unique id for each new conversation, using the browser's built-in method when available, or a random fallback otherwise.
sections.why: Likely reason: some browsers lack the built-in method. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The fallback uses weak randomness, which is acceptable here only because the id is not a secret.

sections.name: AIChatInterface (part 1)
sections.title: Setup, state and consent check
sections.what: Holds the chat state and, on load, asks the server whether AI chat consent is granted. Provides a function to grant consent.
sections.why: The consent check reflects the DPDP consent approach. Reason beyond that not stated.
sections.watch_out: The consent flag starts as granted, so a failed check hides the banner and leaves chat usable. The server must enforce consent.

sections.name: AIChatInterface: if
sections.title: Auto-scroll and conversation list loading
sections.what: Scrolls to the newest message when messages change. Loads the conversation list for the selected patient and opens the most recent one, or starts a new one if none exist.
sections.why: Likely reason: new messages stay visible, and each patient sees their own conversations.
sections.watch_out: If loading the list fails, the page quietly starts a blank conversation, which can hide the problem from the user.

sections.name: AIChatInterface: if
sections.title: Reloading and loading message history
sections.what: Reloads conversations when the patient changes. Loads one conversation's messages, converts them to the display format, and shows a greeting if the history is empty.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the chat tied to the selected patient. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Messages come from the server history, so the server must apply the right patient.

sections.name: AIChatInterface (part 4)
sections.title: Starting and sending questions
sections.what: Starts a blank conversation with a greeting. Selecting one loads its history. Sending shows the question immediately, posts it to the server, then reloads the history and the list.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows questions instantly while keeping the stored history accurate. Reason partly stated by the code's comments.
sections.watch_out: The server's answer is read into a variable but not displayed directly. The page depends on the history reload to show it.

sections.name: AIChatInterface (part 5)
sections.title: Error fallback and sidebar layout
sections.what: On failure, adds a fixed apology message to the chat. Stops the typing indicator. Lays out the sidebar with the conversation list, a loading spinner, an empty note and a New Consultation button.
sections.why: Likely reason: tells the user something went wrong without exposing details. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The real error only goes to the browser console, so users and support staff see only the generic apology.

sections.name: AIChatInterface (part 6)
sections.title: Chat header and message list
sections.what: Shows the assistant's name and status at the top, and lists messages aligned to the sender, with an info button that does nothing yet.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard chat layout. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The info button has no action, and the header claims the assistant is always online, which is fixed text.

sections.name: AIChatInterface (part 7)
sections.title: Source chips and typing indicator
sections.what: Turns each source into a chip that links to its address when one exists, otherwise a plain label. Shows the message time, and three bouncing dots while waiting for a reply.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows where an answer came from. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Source links open in a new tab using addresses supplied by the server, and those addresses are not checked here.

sections.name: AIChatInterface (part 8)
sections.title: Consent banner and starter chips
sections.what: When consent is not granted, shows an amber banner with a button to grant it. Under three messages, shows the starter questions.
sections.why: Likely reason: consent is requested before AI use. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The banner appears only when the consent check has returned not granted, so a slow or failed check hides it.

sections.name: AIChatInterface (part 9)
sections.title: Question input and send button
sections.what: Shows the input box with an attach button, a send button that is disabled when the box is empty, and a disclaimer that the insights are not medical advice.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard chat input. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The attach button does nothing, so users may expect uploads that do not exist. Pressing Enter can send again while a reply is still loading, since there is no guard.

summary: The health assistant chat screen: past conversations on the side, the message list, starter questions and an input box that sends questions to the server.
purpose: Lets a patient ask the assistant questions about their own records and medicines.
why: Likely reason: the consent banner is shown so AI processing happens only with permission. The reason for other parts is not stated.
how: Checks AI chat consent when the page loads. Loads the conversation list for the selected patient and opens the most recent one. Sends each question to the chat endpoint, then reloads the history and conversation list.
inputs: The typed question, the selected patient, and the consent status from the server.
outputs: Messages on screen, and calls to the chat and consent endpoints.
risks: The consent flag starts as granted, so if the check fails the banner does not show and chat remains usable. The reply is received but not shown directly; the page relies on a history reload. The attach button does nothing, and Enter can send while a reply is still loading.
debug: If the list is empty, check the sessions endpoint. If no answer appears, check the chat response field and the history reload. If the consent banner is missing, check the consent status call.
